introduction: North Dakota WIC enrollment starts with an appointment at a local clinic. A caregiver can apply for an eligible child even if the caregiver does not receive WIC.
description: North Dakota WIC enrollment starts with an appointment at a local clinic. A caregiver can apply for an eligible child even if the caregiver does not receive WIC.

sections.who: Pregnancy, recent pregnancy, breastfeeding, infancy or age under five must fit a WIC category. Staff check nutrition needs and income; Medicaid, SNAP or TANF can establish income eligibility.
sections.get: WIC supplies approved foods, nutrition support, breastfeeding guidance and referrals.
sections.docs:
• Identification for each applicant.
  • Address and household income evidence or qualifying benefit records.
  • Infant or child vaccination records requested by the clinic.
sections.apply:
1. Arrange an appointment

    Use the state clinic directory or call 800-472-2286.

  2. Attend with the child

    Enrollment is in person. Bring the infant or child and records the clinic requests.

  3. Complete the nutrition assessment

    Staff review health and nutrition information and explain your food benefits if approved.
sections.after: Keep clinic appointments and ask staff about food substitutions, breastfeeding questions or a change of address.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using WIC categories, Appointment records, Clinic intake, Program services. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Can a father apply for a child?
Yes. WIC welcomes parents and other caregivers of eligible children.
The state says WIC does not require citizenship or immigration-status proof.
Yes, although WIC still assesses the applicable category and nutrition needs.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
